title: cvepatch defensive task manifest (v1)
description: One validated manifest per defensive vulnerability-defense task. Carries the vulnerability semantics, provenance, build + regression commands, and expected baseline/patched results that the trusted grader reads. Distinct from the runner's per-env manifest.schema.json (the image/env record); a task ships both. Missing authoritative facts (CVE, fixed_commit, patch_commit) are represented as null, never invented.

schema_version.description: Defensive task schema version. Bump alongside breaking changes.

cve_id.description: Canonical CVE id, or null when none is assigned/known. Never fabricated.

chromium_issue_id.description: Chromium issue / crbug id, or null.

cwe_ids.description: Associated CWE identifiers. May be empty if unknown.

vulnerable_commit.description: Source revision that exhibits the defect (commit sha or fixture ref).

fixed_commit.description: Upstream fixing commit when independently verified, else null. A commit being linked from an advisory is NOT sufficient to populate this.

source_repository.description: Authoritative source repository URL or local path.

patch_commit.description: Reference/upstream patch commit, or null. Distinct from the agent's candidate patch.

patch_provenance.description: How (and whether) the fixing patch's authenticity is established. 'verified' requires authoritative evidence, not just an advisory link.

status.description: verified = authoritative source + content hash confirmed; claimed = advisory-linked but unconfirmed; unknown = not investigated; absent = no fixing patch exists/known.

build_instructions.description: How to build the candidate. Command argv exec'd in the build worker.

mode.description: dev = fast local build; reproducible = pinned toolchain + recorded digests.

regression_test_command.description: The trusted regression test that encodes the security invariant. null means NO reliable regression oracle exists -> validation can at best be INCONCLUSIVE / MANUAL_REVIEW.

invariant.description: What a PASS means (e.g. 'exit 0 and no ASan report').

existing_test_command.description: Pre-existing functional test suite, to catch unintended behavior changes / test-suppression patches. null = no suite available.

security_checks.description: Optional extra independent checks (additional regression tests, sanitizers, property tests). Cleanliness here is never sufficient on its own.

validation_strategy.description: Which trusted checks are REQUIRED for PATCH_VERIFIED. 'manual_only' = no reliable oracle; result capped at INCONCLUSIVE/MANUAL_REVIEW.

patched_files_allowlist.description: Relative source paths the candidate patch is permitted to touch. Empty = any path under the source subtree (still subject to path-traversal rejection).

expected_baseline_result.description: What the trusted regression test is expected to do on the UNPATCHED baseline. For a reproducible vuln this is 'regression_fail'.

expected_patched_result.description: What the trusted regression test must do on a correctly PATCHED tree for a verified fix.

resource_limits.description: Caps applied to builds/tests inside the worker.

network_policy.description: Network posture during agent execution and validation. 'none' = no outbound network (default).

task_status.description: Lifecycle status of the task definition itself (not a run verdict).

evidence.description: Provenance for every authoritative fact used to construct the task. At least one entry required.

limitations.description: Known limitations of this task (e.g. 'regression oracle is coverage-based, not a true PoC').

metadata.description: Free-form; not interpreted by the grader.
